en: 1. Oṃ. Homage to the illustrious, glorious, and most glorious Mahāgaṇeśa! Homage!
Salutation to the sandals of the venerable Guru. Salutation to the illustrious, illustrious, illustrious Mahābhairava.

Sacrificer’s Flower Vessel. Oṃ. From today onwards... [Statement: For the sacrificer, Mānavagotra Śrī-Śrī-Jayabhūpatīndramallavarman, for the purpose of pleasing the illustrious, illustrious, illustrious Ākāśamahābhairava, this flower vessel is offered in order to perform the five-fold worship (*pañcopacāra-pūjā*) for the weighing ceremony, the consecration, and the universal festival.
I offer.

Within the mandala of Śrī Saṃvartā, the power of bliss is established through the sequential steps; there is the auspicious fourfold emanation, the fivefold group pertaining to Akula and Kula, and another eightfold group.
Furthermore, there are four, another five, and again four—this is the reality according to the mandala.
To that excellent teacher, Bhairava Śrīkujeśa, who is united with [the Goddess], I bow.
Dark-blue and reddish-brown, with three eyes, her breasts heavy with weight, she moves with the gait of an elephant in rut;
her lips are like the bimba fruit, her eyes are beautiful, her hips are broad, and she is adorned with the jewels of a lion's mane.

May she who is known as Śrī Kuvjikā, whose limbs are adorned with celestial raiment, whose beauty is enhanced by exquisite flowers, and whose mass of hair is dark and curly, swiftly bestow upon me the unfailing flood of divine knowledge.
Seated upon the pericarp of a full-blown lotus, she is the supreme Śrī Siddhilakṣmī,
white as camphor, crystal, and the moon, dispelling the darkness of sins;
she always provides a steady boat for crossing the mire-born waters of the ninefold sufferings of saṃsāra.
May she who possesses glorious five lotus-faces, ten arms, and stands upon a corpse protect you.
The Lord, who holds the severed head of Brahmā and the skull of Muṇḍa, who is mounted upon the *uḍamara* tree, and who wields the *khaḍvaṅga* staff raised aloft;
he who is worshipped at his feet by all, including Brahmāṇī and the supreme Mārūkā, is the All-pervading One upon the earth.
The Great Bhairava [entered] the interior of the hollow of the mountain.
May there be success at the commencement of your undertakings; may there be prosperity upon the arrival of wealth;
may there be nourishment for your bodies, and may there be peace in your home.
It pacifies all obstacles, brings about all peace, and is auspicious;
it increases longevity, sons, desire, prosperity, and progeny.
Just as armor serves as a defense against the strikes of arrows,
even so may peace serve as a defense against the decrees of the Creator.
I offer this vessel of flowers.
Nośiya. By means of the threefold truth.
Hrāṃ, svāhā to the principle of the self.
Hrīṃ, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva).
Hūṃ, svāhā to the principle of Śiva!
Homage to the Guru.
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Hsphreṁ Hsauḥ!
Salutation to that venerable Guru who has revealed that state by which the entire universe of moving and non-moving beings is pervaded as an unbroken circle.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, and the Guru is the divine Maheśvara;
the Guru is the entire universe—salutations to that illustrious Guru.
Salutations to the supreme gurus. Salutations to the gurus of the highest state.
Salutations to the supreme teachers and gurus. The sandals for the lotus posture.
To the tortoise-snake, the sandal: *antaṃ lakāyai phaṭ*.
Aiṃ hūṃ phaṭ. O you who are moving yet whose head is unmoving, O you who are of the lineage that is immovable! Hrāṃ hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
The ritual placement (nyāsa).
Aiṃ (5) Hraṃ, Phaṭ to the weapon! This is the purification of the hands.
Hrāṃ, salutation to the little finger; Hrīṃ, svāhā to the ring finger.
Hūṃ, to the middle one, vauṣaṭ!
Hreṃ, salutation to the index finger.
Hroṃ, salutation to the thumb (aguṣṭha). Hraḥ, phaṭ to the weapon (astra). [This is] the ritual placement on the hands (karanyāsa). Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart (hṛdaya).
Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head.
Hūṃ, vauṣaṭ to Śikhī!
Hreṃ, for the armor, hūṃ.
Hrōṃ, vaṣaṭ to the three eyes!
HRAḤ, PHAṬ for the weapon!
Thus ends the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the limbs. Next is the worship of the water vessel (jalapātra).
The sandals for the water-vessel and the seat.
(5) hskṣmlvryūṃ, O Lord of the Heroes, Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda! śkṣmlvryīṃ, the sandals of the venerable Śrījalapātrabhaṭṭārikā!
The six-limbed [rite]; the invocation and so forth; the cow-mudrā; the Gāyatrī.
Hrāṃ! Let us know Śikhinātha; let us meditate upon Svacchanda; may that Rudra inspire us.
The worship of the argha vessel.
The sandals for the seat of the *argha* vessel; [this is] the elephant mudrā together with the *argha* vessel.
Glūṃ slūṃ, the sandals of the venerable lady Māmṛtārghapātra-bhaṭṭārikā.
(5) ŚKMLVRYĪṂ ĀNANDAŚAKTIBHAIRAVĀNANDA VĪRĀDHIPATE HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ, the sandals for the venerable Śrī Arghapātra-bhaṭṭārikā.
The six limbs; the invocation and so forth; the yoni-mudrā; the purification of the elements (bhūta-śuddhi).
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ (***? Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ. Self-Worship: Aiṃ, salutation to sandalwood paste.
Hrīṃ, obeisance to the imperishable triple reality. Śrīṃ, obeisance to the ash of the hero.
Hsphreṃ, homage to the one who deludes all people! Hsauṃ, homage to the various ornaments and flowers!
Hraiḥ! Phaṭ to the weapon! (3) This is the *tāhāppa* worship. Oṃ! Salutation to Gaṅgā!
Oṃ, salutation to Yamunā. Oṃ, salutation to Narmadā. Oṃ, salutation to Kāverī.
Uṃ, obeisance to Kauśikī. Uṃ, obeisance to Gaṇḍakī. Uṃ, obeisance to Sarayū.
Oṃ, salutation to the seven oceans. Oṃ, salutation to the full water-pot.

Hskṣmlvryūṃ! O Kalavṛkṣa, O Great Army-Confounding One, O Sovereign of the Essence of All Mantras, Deities, and Holy Places, O Self of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra, O Essence of the Self, Knowledge, and Śiva—Hskṣmlvryūṃ! To the Lord of the Heroes, Ānandavīra, [who is] the Power of Bliss, Bhairava, and Ānanda.
ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ, homage to the one whose form is the full vase!
Invocation and so forth; the dhenumudrā; the five nectars for the bathing of the deity.
Um, thus it begins; this is the sentence.

The syllable *ū* is the seed-syllable of Vāyu; above that is Varuṇa, and above that is Vajrapāṇi; above that is Ekākala joined with the final letter of the alphabet; and above that is the supreme seed-syllable of Fire, *Haṃsa*.
Seeing each drop of the moon flowing like a stream of milk from the finest white lotuses, Meru, the peak of the Kula, burns perpetually.
Indeed, milk is the very essence of water, and the earth is the very essence of milk.
O Earth, by the command of Śiva, I constantly bathe Kāmadhenu and Śravaṇa.
Dadhicoma-patideva, the beloved favorite of the gods.
And always bathe the deity with excellent water at all times. (Ghera)

By whom was that triple world made auspicious for all people—by the one whose body is purified by clarified butter, who carries the trident purified by his own form, and who, in the guise of a serpent, is Agni himself? Who is he?
Born from the *gomukhī* spear, he is the beloved of the gods;
he stands like a wish-fulfilling tree (*kalpataru*) for those who do not obtain [liberation] through ritual bathing—[O Lord] with the *sākhara*.
They say this fragment is cool to the mind;
the goddess, bathed by the crescent moon, remains unbroken and bestows boons.
I bathe [the deity] with the five products of the cow, perfumed with the five Brahmās and so forth, combined with the five substances, and with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta).
Bathing the eyebrows: ŚKṢMLVRYĪ.
The attendant.
The divine-scented, heart-stealing sandalwood from Śrīkhaṇḍa,
smeared upon the body, is meritorious, purifying, and the destroyer of sins; it is as white as the moon and shines like a mass of pearls.
It constantly brings about prosperity that bestows sovereignty and happiness.
Sindūra.
O Great Heroine, Vīreśvarī! [Behold] the one adorned with the ashes of heroes, who makes the three worlds hear [her name], the Goddess, most excellent and crimson as with vermilion.
Unbroken.
Unbroken, granting inexhaustible desires, and bestowing the attainment of Dharma, desire, and wealth—
grant me exactly what I wish for.
View.
The pure eye of the hero, expanded by the wide gaze of meditation,
is the abode of the moon, sun, and fire, and is the illuminator of all.
The performers of the sacrifice.
The sacrificial thread is the supreme purifier, that which was born of old from Prajāpati;
it is life-prolonging, foremost, matchless, auspicious, and the excellent splendor of the sacrificial thread—may it be yours.
Ahuvāra.
O Supreme Goddess, accept this [seat] whose limbs are variegated with various cloths, fashioned from fine linen,
and most excellent as an ornament for the body of a deity.
Caphamā.
O Lord of Gods, by the gift of this divine parasol, which is like a wish-fulfilling gem and resembles a full moon or sandalwood, grant me the fruit that I have desired.
Bathing.
Māra scatters a rain of various fragrant flowers.
O auspicious lady, this supreme ritual of offering flowers bestows the attainment of good fortune.
The five banners.
The five-colored banner, adorned with beautiful earrings,
consisting of the five elements and made of fine linen, should be displayed.
An ear-flap.
O Supreme Lord, accept this beautiful four-cornered ear-ornament, which has the luster of pure vermilion.
Having offered this [oblation] with the *patavāsanacoya* mantra, one should perform the worship (*jāpūjā*) and the offering (*voya*).
Now, the worship of the deities. Having performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) with the three-layered formula (tritala).
Hrāṃ, svāhā to the principle of the self.
Hrīṃ, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva).
Hūṃ, svāhā to the principle of Śiva.
The Sun’s Arghya: Oṃ, beginning with "adyādi" and so forth. Having extracted the seed-syllable ending in the letter *ra*, one should place Śiva upon it.
But at the beginning, middle, and end, it is adorned with the three fires.
Having illuminated it with the *varman* and likewise with the *sāvitrī*, one should extract [the mantra]:
"The most excellent, singular-peaked one, the Great Māttaṇḍa-Bhairava."
Argha, obeisance. Flower, obeisance.
RHKṢRĪṂ! Salutation to the illustrious Mahāmārttaṇḍa Bhairava.
Homage to the Guru.
Aiṁ (5). Salutation to that venerable Guru by whom the state has been revealed—that which pervades all things moving and unmoving, appearing as an unbroken, undivided sphere.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, and the Guru is the god Maheśvara;
the Guru is indeed the entire universe—to that illustrious Guru, obeisance.
Salutations to the supreme gurus. Salutations to the gurus of the highest state.
Salutations to the supreme teachers and gurus. Valisa. Sandals for Padmāsana.
Pādukā for the tortoise-seat. (5) Va Kha Va Hraḥ, Phaṭ for the weapon. (2)
The face is veiled with the vajra-mudrā.
Aiṃ hūṃ phaṭ! In the vajra-penetrating cage, svāhā!
Touching the ten gates: *calamakule kulahrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*.
Now, the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): (5) *Hraḥ astrāya phaṭ* || 4 || This is the purification of the hands.
Hrāṃ, salutation to Kaniṣṭha.
Hrīṃ, svāhā to the ring finger.
HŪṂ, to the middle one, VAUṢAṬ!
Hreṃ, salutation to the index finger.
Hroṃ, homage to the thumb.
HRAḤ ASTRĀYA PHAṬ. [This is] the Karanyāsa.
Hrāṃ, salutation to the one with the upward-facing mouth.
Hrīṃ, salutation to the eastern face.
Hūṃ, homage to the southern face!
Hreṃ, homage to the northern face.
Hrāṃ, obeisance to the western face.
Hraḥ, salutation to the upward-facing one.
The ritual placement on the face.
Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart.
Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head.
Hūṃ, vaṣaṭ to Śikhī!
The ritual placement on the limbs (aṅganyāsa): the placement of Vatīśinī (vatīśinyāsa).
(5) *Kiṇi* (2), *vicce*, to Koṅkaṇā, *hraḥ*, to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*. This is the purification of the hands (*karasodhana*).
(5) Homage to the Blessed One, she who has taken the lotus; Hrāṃ Śrī, to the big toe, the sandal!
(5) Hsphreṁ, the sandal of Kuvjikā, who dwells on the island of flowers;
Hrīṁ, the sandal of Śrītarjjanī.
(5) Hrāṃ hrīṃ hraṃ, oṃ varvarashikhe hrūṃ, salutation to the venerable Madhyama; [I offer] the sandals.
(5) Ghore, Aghore, Aghoramukhi, Bahurupiye, Hreṃ, to the venerable Anāmikā, [I offer] the sandals.
(5) Cchāṃ cchīṃ to Mahantārikā; hroṃ to Śrīkaniṣṭhā, [I offer] the sandals.
(5) Kini (2) viccai koṅkaṇāyai hraḥ śrīkaratarāya phaṭ, [I worship] the sandals. This is the ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*).
(5) Homage to the Blessed One, she who has taken the lotus [of the heart], Hrāṃ! To the venerable Ūrddhavaktrā, the sandals!
(5) Hsphre, to Kuvjikā, the lamp of the Kula; Hrīṃ, to the eastern face, the sandals! Pādukāṃ!
(5) Hrāṃ hrīṃ hūṃ varvaraśikhe hrūṃ; salutation to the sandals of the glorious right face.
(5) Ghore, Aghore, Aghorāmukhī, Bahurūpāyai, Hreṃ! [I offer] the sandals to the venerable Northern Face.
(5) Chāṃ chīṃ, [salutation] to Mahantārikā; hrāṃ, [salutation to] the venerable Western Face; [offer] the sandals.
Kini (2), to Viccai Koṅkaṇā, Hraḥ, to the venerable Parāparavaktra, [I offer] the sandals.
Vajra-nyāsa.
(5) Homage to the Blessed Lady Hṛtkamalā; Hrāṃ, homage to the glorious Heart.
Hsphreṃ, to Kuvjikā, the lamp of the Kula, Hrīṃ Śrī, to the head, svāhā!
(5) Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, O you with the dark-brown crest! Hūṃ, to the illustrious crest, Voṣaṭ!
(5) Ghore, aghore, aghorāmukhi, bahurūpāyai hreṃ! To the glorious armor, hūṃ!
(5) CCHĀṂ CCHĪṂ to Mahantārīkā; HROṂ VAṢAṬ to the glorious Three Eyes.
Kiṇi vircce moṅkaṇāyai hraḥ astrāye phaṭ.
The ritual placement of the limbs (aṅganyāsa).
The Aghora-nyāsa.
(*)(? To the Great Pāśupata Weapon, Phaṭ! || 4 ||
The purification of the hands.
Aghore hrāḥ, salutation to the two thumbs.
Thaghore Hrīṃ, salutation to the two index fingers.
Hrūṃ pheṃ, salutation to the two middle fingers within the most terrible of the terrible.
To all, everywhere, and everyone: Hreṃ, salutation to the two ring fingers.
Jaṃ saḥ Hrāṃ, to the form of Rudra, salutation to the two little fingers (kaniṣṭhā).
HRAḤ, to the Great Pāśupata Weapon, HRŪṂ PHAṬ; homage to the palms and backs of the hands. [This is the Karanyāsa.]
Aghore hrāṃ, salutation to the heart.
Thaghore hrīṃ, svāhā to the head.
Ghoraghorantare Hrūṃ Phreṃ, Vaṣaṭ to the tuft of hair (śikhā).
Sarvataḥ sarva sarve hreṃ kavacāya hūṃ.
Jaṃ saḥ hrīṃ, to the three eyes in the form of Rudra, vauṣaṭ!
Hraḥ! To the Great Pāśupata Weapon, Hūṃ Phaṭ!
The ritual placement of the limbs (aṅganyāsa).
The worship of the water vessel.
The sandals for the water-vessel and the seat.

(5) *Hskṣmlvryūṃ* Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda, Lord of Heroes (*Vīrādhipati*), *Śkṣmlvryūṃ*. The sandals of the venerable Lady of the Water-Vessel (*Śrījalapātrabhaṭṭārikā*). The six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Invocation and so forth. The Dhenu-mudrā. The Gāyatrī.
Hrāṃ! We know Śikhānātha; we meditate upon Svacchanda; may that Rudra inspire us.
The worship of the argha vessel.
For the purpose of purifying the *argha* vessel, [place] the sandals; [perform] the elephant mudrā for the *argha* vessel.
Glūṃ mlūṃ plūṃ mlūṃ nlūṃ, the sandals of the venerable lady Arghapatrābhaṭṭārikā, who is the supreme immortal.
(5) ŚKMLVRYĪṂ ĀNANDAŚAKTIBHAIRAVĀNANDA ŚRĪMAHĀVIDYĀRĀJEŚVARĪ HSKMLVRYŪṂ | To the venerable Śrī Arghapātra-bhaṭṭārikā, [I offer] the sandals. Three *añjali* salutations. (3)
Hsphreṁ hsphrīṁ hsphrūṁ, the sandals for the venerable Śikhāsvacchanda Mahābhairava.
Glūṃ ga, the sandals for Ratna; mlūṃ, the sandals for Svararatna.
Plūṃ, the sandal for Pātālaratna; Mlūṃ, the sandal for Marttiratna.
nlūṃ (************) (? the sandals. The six limbs. Invocation and so forth. The five mudrās.
The Yonimudrā. Bhūtaśuddhi. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hsauṃ Hsphreṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ.
Self-worship.
Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvrīṃ, for oneself: Aiṃ, sandalwood and the sandals;
[and] the sandals of the venerable Vībhāsmā.
Hsphreṁ, the sandals that enchant all people.
Hsauṃ: various parasols, ornaments, flowers, and sandals.
Having poured [the water] from the argha vessel.
Aiṃ Kuṃ Sauṃ, [the] sandals. (3)
The Mālinī should recite.
Oṃ, salutations to Caṇḍikā. (3) Śrī Bhairava said:

Victory to you, O Goddess Mālinī, stainless and destroyer of impurity! You are the Goddess who is the power of knowledge (*jñāna-śakti*), the intellect (*buddhi*), and the increaser of splendor. You are established as the progenitor of all beings in this worldly existence; O Mother Virāvalī, Goddess, show compassion, O affectionate one!
Victorious is You, the supreme power of knowledge, born from the manifestation of the ultimate reality and Nirvāṇa, consisting of radiant light, emerged in manifest form as the supreme,
auspicious powers of will and action;
again, O Lord, You are the power of sound (nāda), whose form is a straight line and yet possesses the beautiful shape of a coiled serpent-king.

You are celebrated as the radiant one, whose form is light, whose nature is the supreme self, auspicious, named Jyeṣṭhā, Vāmā, Raudrī, and Manonmanī; you are the form of the Bindu, the Avadhūtī, the Half-moon, the Tvaṃtikoṇa, and the syllables Oṃ, Ī, and O joined together— you thus attain the name of Oneness, the embodiment of reality, abiding in the form of the Bhaga.

From the beginning, she is the one whose nature is patience (*kṣāntatva*), whose source-form is her own essential form; she is the awakening of Śrīkaṇṭha, the Mother of Rudra, and likewise the Power of Bliss (*ānandaśakti*). She is the nourisher (*ṛghinī*), whose essence consists of the maintenance of the mass of existence (*bhārabhūti-sthiti-śātmikā*);
she is the pillar-like Sthāṇubhūtā, Harākṣā, Ṛṃṭhiśā, Bhautīśā, and she who is worshipped as Anugraheśā, whose essence is *Sadyojāta*.
You are the consort of Kuleśvara, Maheśvara, and Mahāsena; you are the sixteen-fold nectar that overflows with drops (*bindu*);
you are she who bestows the bliss of supreme liberation and the bliss of ultimate joy upon all those whose bodies are drenched [in grace];
O Bhairavī, you are the power (*śakti*) who sports in the garden of Bhairava; you are Parā Mālinī, the Mother of Rudras, who are worshipped.
Rudraśakti, Khagī, Siddhiyogeśvarī, Siddhimātā, Vibhu, Śabdarāśi, Yoginyārṇavī, Vāgviśuddhā, Śivā, Siddhavāgeśvarī, Mātṛkā, Siddhimatī, Icchā, Kriyā, Maṅgalā, Siddhilakṣmī, [and] Tīrthagati.
You are known as Śāśvatā, Nārāyaṇī, Raktacaṇḍā, Kalālekṣaṇā, Bhīmarūpā, Mahocchuṣmayogapriyā; you are Jayantī, Ajitā, Rudrasaṃhṛtī,
and you are seated upon the lap of the god named Navātman.

O Goddess, you are worshipped by practitioners of the mantra-path who are devoted to the drinking of wine, who are deeply attached to it, and who possess sublime devotion, during the festival of divine drinks with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta). You are the wearer of skulls, the wielder of the khaṭvāṅga staff, and the bearer of the kapāla vessel;
and you are worshipped by those men who have been born one time, twice, thrice, four times, five times, six times, or seven times.
O you who delight in wine and meat, you are gratified by auspicious offerings brought by those resplendent with mantras, vidyās, and vows— namely the muṇḍas,
kaṅkālins, and kāpālikas— who are devoted to divine conduct, and by these classes of ritual utterances: *namaḥ*, *oṃ*, *svāhā*, *svadhā*, *vauṣaṭ*, *vaṣaṭ*, *hūṃ*, and *phaṭ*.

O Goddess, bestower of the yogic powers of the Yoginīs, you are worshipped by practitioners and spiritual sons who utter the syllables of the mantra, by those holding protective threads and rosaries in their left hands, by mothers, by initiates within the maṇḍalas, by yogis gathered in assemblies with hosts of Yoginīs, and by those languid in the play of Rudra.

With eyes like lotus petals and full of affection, you behold her; she is the divine Siddhidevī who dwells in the heavens, the atmosphere, and the seven netherworlds, and who moves through the sky. She remains present for one who recites this *daṇḍaka* with devotion once, twice, or four times a day.

O Goddess, beloved of Mahālakṣmī, even that pure human being who always remembers [the mantra] five, six, seven, or eight times— even he is not stained by fire, weapons, the ocean, or the peak of a mountain,
due to his affection for Your son. O You who are fond of gold, even one who is addicted to stealing gold,
violating another's wife, killing a Brahmin, or killing a cow, or one who is wicked with great faults, is purified.

Remembering your face— which resembles the full moon and possesses a shimmering divine ruby as its radiant forehead-mark polished by noble hands— even those whose arms, thighs, and toes are bound with firm serpent-nooses are liberated through the chanting of your name.

O Goddess Mahākālī, O you whose splendor is like the fire of time (Kālāgni), those who remember your two lotus feet are released from terrible and great diseases by Skanda, Brahmā, Indra, the Moon, the Sun, and the Flower-armed One (Kāmadeva), [who are present] with garlands of bees upon their heads and the filaments of blooming lotuses.
O Piñjarasarvavīrāmbikā, O Bhairavī; I have come to you, O Bhairava, for refuge.
Forgive my transgression, forgive my transgression, O Śivā!
Thus, O Goddess, by the great-souled Bhairava,
the Supreme Goddess then emerged from the Liṅga in Vinibhadra.
Thus ends the Mālinī-daṇḍaka hymn.
O Āvāhāhikṣa, I invoke you here. [Then follows] the five-fold offering (pañcavali).
The pair was enveloped in a mass of blazing flames.
The sandals for the sake of the gods.
Śrīṃ Hrāṃ, the sandals for Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha.
Obeisance! [I offer] sandals to Narāsana.
(5) Then, [he offers] the sandals to the goddess Prastaradīpāmbhikī and to the Mahādhvāṅkṣa Kṣetrapāla.
Vali.
The sandals for the lion-throne; the sandals for the yoginīs; the offering.
